trust_services_criteria.quote: trust services criteria relevant to security, availability, confidentiality, and privacy (applicable trust services criteria)

3.1.1.quote: This service also offers transport encryption to enhance data confidentiality in transit. Google uses encryption to secure user data in transit between Google production facilities.

supporting_quotes.quote: Machine-level access restriction relies on Google-developed distributed authentication service based on Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificates which helps to positively identify the resource access requester.
85. The organization uses encryption to secure user data in transit between the organization's production facilities. CC6.7 ... No deviations noted.
59. Encryption is used to protect user authentication and administrator sessions transmitted over the Internet. CC6.1, CC6.6, CC6.7

3.1.1.notes: Real standard: TLS/SSL-based encryption in transit; the report never names a specific TLS version (no 'TLS 1.2' or 'TLS 1.3' anywhere in the text). If a version-specific dropdown is preferred it cannot be supported from this report.

3.1.2.quote: 51. Customer data that is uploaded or created is encrypted at rest. CC6.1 ... Inspected the encryption configuration for storage devices with customer data at rest and determined that encryption was enabled. No deviations noted.

supporting_quotes.quote: Google hard drives leverage technologies such as Full Disk Encryption (FDE) and drive locking, to protect data at rest.
All traffic is at least cryptographically authenticated between machines, while some connections, including to and from the Key Management Service, are encrypted using AES.

3.1.2.notes: Real standard as documented: encryption at rest is an audited control (control 51, no deviations) and hard drives use Full Disk Encryption, but no cipher/key length (e.g. AES-256) is stated. The only AES mention (p. 225) is in Section V 'Other Information Provided by Google LLC', which the auditor explicitly did not examine, and it concerns internal traffic, not at-rest data. Do not write 'AES-256' from this report.

3.1.4.quote: Google uses a proprietary service to manage the distribution, generation and rotation of cryptographic keys. Files or data structures with user-generated content written by Cloud or App Engine services are encrypted with a key.

supporting_quotes.quote: Cloud KMS is a cloud-hosted key management service that manages encryption for cloud services. It enables the generation, use, rotation, and destruction of encryption keys.
Cloud EKM lets customers encrypt data in Google Cloud Platform with encryption keys that are stored and managed in a third-party key management system deployed outside Google's infrastructure.
Cloud HSM is a cloud-hosted Hardware Security Module (HSM) service for hosting encryption keys and performing cryptographic operations.

3.1.4.notes: Default: Google's proprietary key management service generates and rotates keys (key rotation at least every 90 days on average, p. 225 — Section V, unaudited). Customer-controlled options exist as in-scope services: Cloud KMS (customer-managed keys, CMEK-style), Cloud HSM, and Cloud EKM (customer keys held outside Google — BYOK/external key support), all p. 35.

3.1.8.line: Two-factor authentication for remote and sensitive-system access
3.1.8.quote: Access to sensitive systems and applications requires two-factor authentication in the form of unique user IDs, strong passwords, security keys, and/or certificates.

3.1.8.line: Vulnerability management program with regular analysis
3.1.8.quote: Google has developed vulnerability management guidelines and regularly analyzes the vulnerabilities associated with the system environment.

3.1.8.line: Data-center physical security: guards, badges, cameras, 24x7 security personnel
3.1.8.quote: Existence of security guards, access badges, and video cameras ... Video cameras exist to monitor the interior and exterior of the facility ... 24 x 7 on-site security personnel

3.1.8.line: Access to internal support tools restricted via ACLs; periodic access reviews
3.1.8.quote: Access to internal support tools ... is controlled via Access Control Lists (ACLs) thus limiting the use of these tools to only those individuals that have been specifically authorized.
The data centers are connected through multiple encrypted network links and interfaces.

3.1.8.line: Verified disk erasure and physical destruction of retired drives
3.1.8.quote: When a hard drive is retired, authorized individuals verify that the disk is erased by writing zeros to the drive and performing a multiple-step verification process.

3.1.8.line: DDoS detection with incident response processes
3.1.8.quote: identify distributed denial of service (DDOS) attacks. Google has established incident response processes to report and handle such events.

3.2.1.quote: Europe, Middle East, and Africa: Berlin (1), Germany ... Dublin, Ireland; Eemshaven, Groningen, The Netherlands; Frankfurt (1), Hesse, Germany ... Fredericia, Denmark; Ghlin, Hainaut, Belgium; Hamina, Finland
3.2.1.notes: In-scope data center list includes numerous EU locations (Germany, Ireland, Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, Finland, Spain, Italy, Sweden). EU data-center presence is stated; the report does not itself describe an 'EU Access'/sovereignty contractual program.

absent_notes.3.1.3: Backups are mentioned only as customer products (Google Cloud Backup and DR, Backup for GKE, pp. 34, 39), a customer responsibility for non-Google systems (p. 67), and backup-data deletion after retention (p. 134). No encryption standard for Google's own backups is stated.
absent_notes.3.1.6: No occurrence of 'anonymize'/'anonymization' anywhere in the report text.
